title: What counts as hand hygiene?
banner: DRAFT, NOT clinically reviewed. Original practical exercise with fictional people; never imported, published or shown to learners.
gaps: No published exercise may exist until the review phase: this is a specification only.
The wording, answers and explanations are the author's reading of the cited sources and have had no clinical or educational review.

sources.use: CDC healthcare-worker hand hygiene page (2024): targeted indications, glove use, definition and product safety sections inspected.

required_sources: WHO or national hand hygiene guidance read in full
setup: A fictional shift on a fictional ward.

items.text: Washing hands with water and soap
items.why: Soap and water are required when hands are visibly soiled. Other indications depend on local infection-prevention policy.

items.text: Cleaning hands with an alcohol-based hand rub
items.why: Alcohol-based rub is preferred in most routine healthcare situations when hands are not visibly soiled; follow outbreak-specific and local infection-prevention guidance.

items.text: Wiping hands on a clean towel without soap or rub
items.why: It is not one of the listed methods of cleaning hands.

items.text: Putting on new gloves without cleaning the hands
items.why: Gloves do not replace hand hygiene. Clean hands before donning when required and after removing gloves.
